reading.body:
Browser-use leads the open-source coding and browser agent ecosystem with 112,000 stars, but the category remains fragmented across five major projects with no dominant standard.

The field splits into two tracks. Browser agents like browser-use and stagehand automate web interactions, treating the internet as a programmable interface for AI. Coding agents like cline, aider, and continue embed AI directly into developer workflows as assistants or autonomous contributors. Both depend on the same constraint: the model must reliably perceive and act on external systems without human intervention between steps, which demands compute capable of running inference fast enough to make real-time decisions practical.

The active maintenance across all five projects, with pushes within days of the data collection date, suggests the category is still evolving rapidly. None has achieved the kind of consolidation around a single platform seen in other infrastructure layers. For AI scaling, this means the bottleneck is not yet these agents themselves, but the underlying model performance and inference speed they require to function reliably at scale.

This data covers open-source repositories only. It does not capture proprietary agents from major AI labs, commercial offerings, or internal tool use within enterprises, all of which may represent substantial deployed capacity outside this view.
